correctness.rationale: A finite member A of F yields the least nonempty member H=intersection of the finite trace; L and R reduce to a single finite intersection over h∈H. If F lacks a least member, K=intersection F is not large; D_x={A∈F:x∉A}, x∉K, have finite-intersection property, so an ultrafilter on Y=F extends all D_x. Membership relation x∈A gives every column in F while the G-large-row set equals K and fails F. If F is generated by infinite H, a free ultrafilter on H and off-diagonal incidence give the opposite failure. The three cases are exhaustive in ZFC; finite test script enumerates proper filters of carriers ≤3 but infinite proof is symbolic.
